title: The tenth of Muharram
hook: Husayn and his companions and family are killed on the day of Ashura

segments.voice: Yesterday: Karbala, a camp within sight of the Euphrates, and soldiers between them and the water. Your line was they were thirsty.

Before Karbala, the tenth day of Muharram already had a name: Ashura. Bukhari records that when the Prophet, peace be upon him, came to Medina, he found the Jews of the city fasting on that day, remembering how God had saved Moses and his people. The Prophet fasted it too, and asked his followers to fast. So it was a day of rescue, kept with a fast. Then came a morning on a plain beside the Euphrates, and the same day gained a second memory, this one of grief.
screen: `ASHURA ALREADY HAD A NAME.` → `A DAY OF RESCUE.` → `THEN A SECOND MEMORY.`

segments.voice: The histories tell the morning slowly, and it is right to tell it plainly. Husayn's small band faces the army. One man rides out from the army's ranks and crosses over: al-Hurr, the commander who first blocked Husayn's road, whose horses Husayn had watered. He asks if there is any repentance for him, and fights at Husayn's side. Then, through the day, the companions fall one by one. Then the young men of the family: sons, nephews, brothers. Tradition counts seventy-two in all who died with him. And at the last, Husayn himself, thirsty, is killed. The women and children are taken captive, among them his sister Zaynab, and his son Ali, who was too sick to fight. Sunni and Shia Muslims both honor Husayn. Sunni Muslims honor him as the Prophet's grandson, and Sunni practice keeps the Ashura fast from the Prophet's own example. For Shia Muslims, Husayn is the third Imam, and the tenth is the center of the year's mourning: gatherings, elegies, tears, the story told again so that it is never told for the last time. The Qur'an speaks to those who fall in God's way. In Pickthall's translation: "And call not those who are slain in the way of Allah 'dead.' Nay, they are living, only ye perceive not." Shia tradition reads Karbala in the light of that verse. One date carries two memories, a people rescued and a family falling, and both are kept.
screen: `AL-HURR CROSSES OVER.` · `ONE BY ONE, THEN HUSAYN.` · `SUNNI AND SHIA BOTH HONOR HIM.` · `NAY, THEY ARE LIVING.` · then, large: `THE TENTH DAY.`

segments.voice: There's nothing to fix in this one. Let the names you heard come and go, al-Hurr, al-Abbas, Zaynab, Husayn, and keep them company a while, the way people sit with a family after a death. If you pray, you can say, as the Qur'an teaches, we are Allah's and unto Him we are returning; if you don't, just keep the quiet.
Ashura. The tenth day of Muharram: the day the Prophet fasted for Moses' rescue, and the day Husayn and his companions were killed at Karbala. Today's word.
Your line: the tenth day. Rest gently with it, and with all of them. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: On the tenth of Muharram, Shia Muslims gather to mourn Husayn with elegies and recitations of Karbala; Sunni Muslims honor him too, and Sunni communities keep the Ashura fast that the Prophet kept.
